old: To Roman anatomists, a flexing body part looked like a small animal moving just beneath the skin.
That resemblance is Latin for “little mouse” — the nickname stuck so well it became the official word for it.
The same Latin root for “mouse” gives us the small rodent itself, and much later, the computer accessory named after it.
clues: This part of the body gets its name from a Latin word meaning "little mouse," an image the Romans saw in it.
The general name for the body tissue that contracts to move your bones, which weightlifters build up; not the tendon that anchors it, nor any single one like the bicep.
You might pull one at the gym, and hired tough guys are called this. Its ancient root also gave us the word mouse, and later the computer mouse.
